text:
mike: Quick recap from last night's ~2m p99 spike (00:42 UTC). Root cause appears to be an autoscaler race where the scale-down step removed a hot bucket while warmups were still in flight. No customer SLA breaches detected but a handful of requests hit 10s+ latency.

anya: Thanks for the summary. Do we have an immediate mitigation to stop this repeating during higher traffic periods?

mike: Short-term mitigation: increase scale-down grace to 5m and require KV warmup confirmation before finalizing drain. I've updated the emergency runbook with the steps.

devon: Can you paste the specific policy change? ops wants a one-liner to apply via orchestration.

mike: Sure. Policy patch (orchestrator CLI):

```
infractl autoscaler update --pool=edge-hot --scale-down-grace=300s --min-ready-check=kv-warm
```

mike: Also tagging a new boolean on the drain flow: drain.wait_for_kv=true.

anya: Good. How does this affect our SLOs and paging thresholds? We want to avoid noisy pages during the config flip.

mike: For the window where we roll the mitigation (now -> +30m), silence the latency-noise channel and change the p99 page rule to 8s for 10m sustained. We'll revert alerts after verification.

devon: What about incident review /postmortem? Are we changing service-level targets?

mike: Postmortem posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/autoscaler-race-2051. TL;DR: no SLO target change yet, but we will update the SLO doc to include a "warmup-safe drain" clause and add an SRE-owned acceptance test for every autoscaler change.

anya: Any customer-facing communication needed?

mike: No external comms required; no SLA breaches and root cause internal. I'll notify CS privately if anything changes.

sre-bot: Reminder scheduled: apply autoscaler patch in 15m and post verification metrics to #eng-sre thread.

devon: One request: can we add a small canary rolling drain for Dedicated pools with reserved capacity tagging? want to make sure reserved capacity logic isn't impacted.

mike: Yes — canary plan: target non-prod Dedicated pool tagged 'canary-dedicated', run one partial drain, run kv-warmup, measure tail latency for 10m, then proceed. Commands are in the runbook.

anya: Also proposing a new maintenance policy update: require autoscaler changes to run the "warmup acceptance" test in staging and have SRE signoff for prod rollouts. It's in the draft PR.

mike: Agreed. Assigning owner: devon will shepherd the PR.

devon: ack. I'll get the PR merged today and schedule the staged test.

mike: After we finish the mitigation rollout I'll open a small maintenance window next week to run a controlled failover drill (15m) to validate the fix under load. Tentative: Tue 06:00 UTC. Will announce separately.

anya: ack :thumbsup:

devon: ack

mike: Closing loop: mitigation applied. Will monitor p95/p99 and error-rate for 1h. If anything unexpectedly degrades, escalate to pagerduty.

pagerduty-bot: On-call escalation policy: if >3 critical pages in 30m, escalate to SRE lead.

sre-bot: Post-run summary request: please paste the p95/p99 numbers and a short note in this thread when done.
